rules.description: Fuel trim saturated — positive (max enrichment): ECU has adapted fuel trims to maximum positive limit, adding fuel against a perceived lean condition that contradicts the gas analyser. Long-term and short-term trims both pegged high. Typically accompanied by P0171 (System Too Lean) but the gas analyser shows rich or stoichiometric — the ECU is being deceived. Truth-vs-perception: ECU perceives lean, gas analyser shows rich or normal. v1 orphan ERR-EF-001 (fuel_trim_saturated) reactivated, positive polarity
rules.precondition: longft1 and shrtft1 prefer live OBD (OBDLivePayload), fall back to freeze-frame

rules.description: Fuel trim saturated — negative (max enleanment): ECU has adapted fuel trims to maximum negative limit, pulling fuel against a perceived rich condition that contradicts the gas analyser. Long-term and short-term trims both pegged low. Typically accompanied by P0172 (System Too Rich) but the gas analyser shows lean or stoichiometric — the ECU is being deceived by a biased sensor. Truth-vs-perception: ECU perceives rich, gas analyser shows lean or normal. v1 orphan ERR-EF-001 (fuel_trim_saturated) reactivated, negative polarity
rules.precondition: longft1 and shrtft1 prefer live OBD (OBDLivePayload), fall back to freeze-frame

rules.description: Closed-loop fuel control disabled / trims frozen: ECU has disabled closed-loop fuel control — both long-term and short-term fuel trims are frozen at or near zero because the ECU cannot trust its sensor inputs. Accompanied by DTCs indicating ECU-level faults (P0606 ECU internal), sensor circuit faults that force open-loop (P0113 IAT circuit high, P0118 ECT circuit high), injector driver faults (P0201-P0206), or coolant thermostat faults (P0128). The ECU has given up adapting — the trims tell the story. v1 orphan ERR-EF-002 (closed_loop_fuel_control_disabled) reactivated
rules.precondition: longft1 and shrtft1 prefer live OBD (OBDLivePayload), fall back to freeze-frame

rules.description: ECU internal fault — DTC-driven: ECU has logged an internal hardware or software fault (P0600-P0699 range, ECU_INTERNAL_HISTORY). These are processor, memory, or calibration integrity faults detected by the ECU's own self-diagnostics. TIMING_RETARDED chemistry may appear as a secondary symptom when the ECU limits ignition timing in response to the internal fault (~10 ecu_fault cases produce this chemistry in the curated corpus). No OBD gate — the ECU internal DTC alone gates this rule. This is the only ecu_fault rule that carries a chemistry evidence slot (TIMING_RETARDED SUGGESTIVE), closing the Tier B gap for ecu_fault

SAMPLE_INVALID with ECU fault: GASLab's triangle-gate rejects the sample as unphysical (CO+CO2+O2 outside [14,16]), typically because the ECU fault has corrupted sensor data or caused a measurement anomaly. SAMPLE_INVALID chemistry gates this rule — it only evaluates when GASLab emits SAMPLE_INVALID. When the triangle fails AND ECU-fault-indicative DTCs are present (P0171/P0172 fuel trim codes or P0606 ECU internal), the unphysical gas reading is attributed to ECU control failure rather than an analyser problem. Covers the ~2 SAMPLE_INVALID ecu_fault cases identified in the chemistry coverage matrix
